Yes—for the bug your closed [#9839](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/9839) attempted to solve, [#12771](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/12771) is a more complete implementation. It was merged on September 4.

| Area | Your #9839 | Merged #12771 |
|---|---|---|
| Stale mise symlink but missing rustup toolchain | Detected via rustup filesystem layout | Detected through authoritative `rustup component list` queries |
| Explicit components/targets | Checked internal files/directories with name heuristics | Uses `rustup ... list --installed --toolchain` |
| `profile = "default"` | Checked `clippy` and `rustfmt` | Checks `clippy`, `rust-docs`, and `rustfmt` |
| Omitted profile | Not reconciled | Runs `rustup show profile` and respects the effective profile |
| Repairing existing toolchains | Relied mostly on `--profile default` | Explicitly passes missing default components, because rustup ignores profile expansion on an existing toolchain |
| Prompt/hook performance | Proposed an install-only check | Preserves cheap marker checks for `hook-env`; deeper checks run only during install-related decisions |
| Coverage | Explicit install-focused paths | Explicit install, auto-install, lazy providers, dry-run, and post-install refresh |

The core approach is:

1. Normal interactive operations still ask only, “does mise’s install marker exist?”
2. Install-related operations ask the backend’s deeper `is_install_satisfied` predicate.
3. For Rust, that predicate validates the symlink target and asks rustup about the selected toolchain, components, targets, and effective profile.
4. If anything is missing, mise reruns `rustup toolchain install`, explicitly supplying the default-profile components needed to repair an existing toolchain.

That separation is the important architectural improvement. Your PR manually reconstructed rustup’s internal state from `settings.toml`, toolchain directories, and `lib/rustlib/components`. Reviewers found edge cases in that logic, including missing component metadata and guessed `-preview` names. #12771 lets rustup describe its own state instead, while keeping those subprocesses away from shell-prompt paths. See the merged [Rust satisfaction check](https://github.com/jdx/mise/blob/3942985b71929476f73276c9eca984ff1daa3f00/src/plugins/core/rust.rs#L322-L399) and [repair logic](https://github.com/jdx/mise/blob/3942985b71929476f73276c9eca984ff1daa3f00/src/plugins/core/rust.rs#L515-L550).

What is still not done:

- Selective `mise-action` cache paths/exclusions were not implemented. [mise-action #612](https://github.com/jdx/mise-action/issues/612) remains open. #12771 fixes correctness when rustup state is excluded or absent; it does not provide fine-grained cache controls.
- The special implicit-component reconciliation only models rustup’s `default` profile. A partially damaged `complete`-profile toolchain is not exhaustively checked unless its components are explicitly configured. This was also outside #9839’s actual implementation.
- It is merged but not yet released. The latest release is still [v2026.9.1](https://github.com/jdx/mise/releases/tag/v2026.9.1), which predates the merge. #12771 is listed in the open [v2026.9.2 release PR](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/12692).

So: nothing material from #9839’s intended bug-fix scope appears missing, and #12771 closes several gaps in it. The only pending practical step is the v2026.9.2 release; selective caching and exhaustive `complete`-profile validation remain separate concerns.

I’ll verify the exact distinction between mise’s `profile` option and rustup’s supported profile names, then relate it to #12771’s reconciliation behavior.

Yes—but “custom profile” can mean two different things:

- Selecting a non-default rustup profile: mise supports `profile = "minimal"`, `"default"`, or `"complete"`.
- Defining an arbitrary named profile: no. Rustup itself only supports those three profile names; mise passes the value through to rustup.

For #12771:

- Explicit `profile = "minimal"` is honored.
- If `profile` is omitted, mise runs `rustup show profile`, so a profile selected using `rustup set profile minimal` is honored.
- `profile = "default"` gets special reconciliation: mise verifies and repairs `clippy`, `rust-docs`, and `rustfmt`.
- `profile = "complete"` works for a new installation, but #12771 does not enumerate and reconcile every component implied by `complete`.
- A custom component combination is fully supported and reconciled:

```toml
[tools]
rust = {
  version = "1.83.0",
  profile = "minimal",
  components = ["rust-src", "llvm-tools"],
  targets = ["wasm32-unknown-unknown"],
}
```

So my earlier wording should be refined: mise supports choosing a profile and building a customized toolchain with explicit components. The remaining limitation is specifically reconstructing all implicit components of the `complete` profile on an already-installed toolchain. Rustup documents that profiles affect only newly installed toolchains, which is why #12771 must explicitly repair default-profile components. See [mise’s Rust documentation](https://github.com/jdx/mise/blob/3942985b71929476f73276c9eca984ff1daa3f00/docs/lang/rust.md#L114-L156) and [rustup’s profile behavior](https://github.com/rust-lang/rustup/blob/master/doc/user-guide/src/concepts/profiles.md).

## Summary

- reconcile all components implied by the `minimal`, `default`, or `complete` Rust profile when a rustup toolchain already exists
- restore removable base components such as `rustc`, `cargo`, and the host `rust-std`, as well as profile extensions
- distinguish host components from same-named cross-target components and support rustup's `m`, `d`, and `c` aliases
- tolerate missing, malformed, and legacy profileless installed manifests without turning metadata inspection into an install error
- document that rustup has only three named profiles; custom sets use mise's `components` and `targets` options

## Context and approach

This follows #12771. That PR made the default profile's optional components explicit, but a rustup source audit showed the gap is broader: profiles are applied only while creating a toolchain, and rustup allows required components such as `rustc` to be removed afterward.

For an existing toolchain, mise now:

1. uses `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=<requested>` with `rustup show active-toolchain` to obtain rustup's canonical host-qualified toolchain name without depending on `rustc` being installed
2. reads the installed `lib/rustlib/multirust-channel-manifest.toml` with a small typed schema
3. follows rustup's own profile lookup against the selected host's required and extension components, including reverse rename mapping from internal `*-preview` package names to public component names
4. compares public component names only with bare installed names or names qualified by that exact host
5. passes the resolved profile components explicitly to `rustup toolchain install`, making rustup repair an already-present toolchain

Relevant rustup behavior:

- [profiles are only supplied when creating a toolchain](https://github.com/rust-lang/rustup/blob/60e495a99dc409c13c52dff1889217f5f9a1ae61/src/dist/mod.rs#L908-L928)
- [profile membership is resolved through the selected host target](https://github.com/rust-lang/rustup/blob/60e495a99dc409c13c52dff1889217f5f9a1ae61/src/dist/manifest.rs#L372-L401)
- [the supported profile names and aliases are minimal/m, default/d, and complete/c](https://github.com/rust-lang/rustup/blob/60e495a99dc409c13c52dff1889217f5f9a1ae61/src/dist/mod.rs#L753-L801)

Rustup has no public command that reports profile membership, so the installed manifest is the source of truth. If it cannot be read, mise uses stable minimal/default fallbacks; complete falls back to rustup's native handling rather than guessing a release-dependent component set.

- restore removable base components such as `rustc`, `cargo`, and the host `rust-std`, as well as profile extensions

## Context and approach

This follows #12771. That PR made the default profile's optional components explicit, but a rustup source audit showed the gap is broader: profiles are applied only while creating a toolchain, and rustup allows required components such as \`rustc\` to be removed afterward.

For an existing toolchain, mise now:

1. uses \`RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=<requested>\` with \`rustup show active-toolchain\` to obtain rustup's canonical host-qualified toolchain name without depending on \`rustc\` being installed

2. `fix(rust): derive profile components from rustup metadata` → PR 1

   - Resolve release-specific profile membership and renamed components.
   - Support `m`, `d`, and `c` aliases.
   - Add valid-manifest `complete` reconciliation and legacy-manifest coverage.
   - Document that rustup has no arbitrary named custom profiles; custom sets use mise `components` and `targets`.

3. `fix(rust): recover complete profile metadata` → PR 2

   - Keep existing PR [#12786](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/12786) for this top layer.
   - Recover missing/malformed installed metadata using the exact channel manifest.
